      "title": "Batch construction exceeds the API's 256-record limit",

      "recommendation": "Use API_BATCH_LIMIT for batch sizing and add tests asserting every batch respects the 256-record cap, including inputs of 256, 257, and 1,000 records."
    },
    {
      "severity": "high",
      "title": "Eager materialization violates the bounded-memory guarantee",
      "body": "list(records) consumes the entire iterable, then the comprehension retains every batch simultaneously. A tracemalloc probe with only one million integer records peaked at 48,231,720 bytes, already exceeding the claimed 4 MB for ten million. Large inputs can exhaust memory before any batch reaches the caller.",
      "file": "docs/audits/fixtures/metrics-batcher/batcher.py",
      "line_start": 17,
      "line_end": 18,
      "confidence": 1.0,
      "recommendation": "Yield batches incrementally from the input iterator. Update callers/tests for lazy consumption and verify that requesting the first batch consumes only one batch of input."
    },
    {
      "severity": "medium",
      "title": "Rounding admits allocations at the forbidden reserve boundary",
      "body": "check_quota_split([0.3, 0.3, 0.3]) returns 0.10000000000000009 and passes, although three 30% shares leave exactly 10%, which the contract excludes. The equivalent [0.9] allocation raises. The existing equal-shares test enshrines this inconsistent boundary behavior.",
      "file": "docs/audits/fixtures/metrics-batcher/batcher.py",
      "line_start": 24,
      "line_end": 25,
      "confidence": 0.99,
      "recommendation": "Define quota precision and use exact decimal or integer units for the comparison. Require both 90% allocation representations to raise, and test reserves immediately above and below the boundary."
    }
  ],
  "next_steps": [
    "Fix batch sizing, introduce lazy batching, and enforce a consistent quota boundary; rerun tests covering these counterexamples."
  ]
}

result.summary: Do not ship: batch sizes exceed the declared API cap, memory grows with the entire input, and floating-point rounding bypasses the strict reserve boundary. All five existing tests pass despite these failures.

findings.title: Batch construction exceeds the API's 256-record limit
findings.body: Both the slice width and stride use 265. Reproduced: 257 records produce one 257-record batch; 1,000 produce lengths [265, 265, 265, 205]. These exceed the documented cap and would be rejected by the API.
findings.recommendation: Use API_BATCH_LIMIT for batch sizing and add tests asserting every batch respects the 256-record cap, including inputs of 256, 257, and 1,000 records.

findings.title: Eager materialization violates the bounded-memory guarantee
findings.body: list(records) consumes the entire iterable, then the comprehension retains every batch simultaneously. A tracemalloc probe with only one million integer records peaked at 48,231,720 bytes, already exceeding the claimed 4 MB for ten million. Large inputs can exhaust memory before any batch reaches the caller.
findings.recommendation: Yield batches incrementally from the input iterator. Update callers/tests for lazy consumption and verify that requesting the first batch consumes only one batch of input.

findings.title: Rounding admits allocations at the forbidden reserve boundary
findings.body: check_quota_split([0.3, 0.3, 0.3]) returns 0.10000000000000009 and passes, although three 30% shares leave exactly 10%, which the contract excludes. The equivalent [0.9] allocation raises. The existing equal-shares test enshrines this inconsistent boundary behavior.
findings.recommendation: Define quota precision and use exact decimal or integer units for the comparison. Require both 90% allocation representations to raise, and test reserves immediately above and below the boundary.

next_steps: Fix batch sizing, introduce lazy batching, and enforce a consistent quota boundary; rerun tests covering these counterexamples.
